record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.context_brief: Positive scalar curvature on aspherical manifolds
record.original_question: Can an aspherical closed smooth manifold admit a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature, or does every such manifold necessarily fail to admit one?

evidence.quote: An aspherical closed smooth manifold does not admit a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A closed smooth manifold $M$ is called aspherical if its universal cover is contractible (equivalently, $\pi_k(M)=0$ for all $k\ge 2$). A Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ has positive scalar curvature if its scalar curvature function $\operatorname{Scal}_g$ is everywhere strictly positive.

Question: Does there exist a closed aspherical smooth manifold $M$ that admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature? Equivalently, prove or disprove the following conjecture: every closed aspherical smooth manifold fails to admit any Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.
artifact.category_tag: Positive scalar curvature on aspherical manifolds
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (often attributed to Gromov–Lawson) that no closed aspherical manifold admits a metric of positive scalar curvature is known to hold in dimensions ≤ 5 (dimension 3 by Gromov–Lawson and Perelman; dimensions 4 and 5 by recent work using generalized soap bubbles / μ-bubbles, e.g. Chodosh–Li and Gromov). It remains open in dimensions ≥ 6.

status_evidence.title: Recent results concerning topological obstructions to PSC (survey, Chodosh)
status_evidence.snippet: For n ∈ {4,5}, a closed aspherical n-manifold does not admit a Riemannian metric with positive scalar curvature.
status_evidence.claim: Settled in dimensions 4 and 5; open in higher dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Generalized soap bubbles and the topology of manifolds with PSC
status_evidence.snippet: Closed aspherical n-manifolds, n ∈ {4,5}, do not admit metrics of positive scalar curvature.

status_evidence.title: Gromov-Lawson conjecture - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: For aspherical manifolds, Gromov's conjecture: an aspherical manifold cannot carry a metric with positive scalar curvature.
